speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; please tell me, when did these symptoms first start, and have they been getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; when you say "recently," do you mean this started within the last few months, and is the clumsiness on the right side constant or does it fluctuate? Also, have you noticed any weakness, numbness, or double vision accompanying these gait issues?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very important detail; given your history of Crohn's disease and your use of natalizumab, we must immediately rule out Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). REQUEST TEST: MRI of the brain with and without contrast. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain.
